evals.prompt: I want AI to help me draft replies to my emails. I get about 30 emails a day and it takes me forever to respond. Can you help me set this up?
evals.expected_output: Correctly classified as Tier 0, Profile 0 (Assistant). Produces an Agent Brief — NOT a squad topology. Brief includes: role definition, event-driven trigger (inbound email), in-context memory, approval gate before sending, escalation conditions for sensitive emails, tone instructions.
expectations: The skill classifies this as Tier 0 — single agent, no topology needed
The skill identifies Profile 0: Assistant
The skill does NOT propose a squad topology or BlockDiag
The skill produces an Agent Brief document
The Agent Brief includes an explicit approval gate — agent drafts but does not send autonomously
The Agent Brief includes escalation conditions (e.g., legal/financial content, tier-1 clients)
The Agent Brief includes tone and voice instructions
The Agent Brief includes an evolution path section noting when this might grow into Tier 1
The skill asks at most 3-4 clarifying questions before producing the brief

evals.prompt: We run a recruitment agency. We need agents to: find candidates on LinkedIn, screen their CVs against job requirements, schedule interviews with hiring managers, and send rejection emails to unsuccessful candidates. This all needs to be coordinated.
evals.expected_output: Correctly classified as Tier 1, multiple profiles (Researcher + Executor + Orchestrator). Routes to Squad Topologies. Identifies 3-4 stream-aligned squads (sourcing, screening, scheduling, communications), an orchestrator, and a platform. DDD augmentation noted for candidate data model.
expectations: The skill classifies this as Tier 1 — multi-squad topology required
The skill identifies multiple profiles: Researcher (sourcing), Executor (screening, scheduling, comms), Orchestrator (coordination)
The skill asks the LeSS question — could one generalist agent do this? — and correctly concludes no
The skill identifies at least 3 distinct value streams
The skill routes to Squad Topologies Architect facilitation
The skill notes DDD as relevant augmentation (candidate data shared across squads)
The skill produces a squad map with at least 4 squads
The skill produces a squad-topology.diag in valid BlockDiag syntax
The skill produces a squad-registry.md
The skill identifies interaction modes between squads

evals.prompt: We're a fintech company. We need AI agents to process loan applications — extract data from documents, run credit checks via our API, make preliminary approval decisions, flag edge cases for human review, and log everything for our compliance audit trail.
evals.expected_output: Correctly classified as Tier 1 with SAFe augmentation. Profiles include Executor (document processing), Validator (credit + decision), Sentinel (edge case flagging). SAFe layer is load-bearing for audit trail and compliance. Human-in-the-loop is mandatory for edge cases.
expectations: The skill classifies this as Tier 1 with SAFe augmentation — not just Squad Topologies alone
The skill explicitly flags the compliance/audit requirement as changing the design
The skill identifies Profile 4: Validator for the credit check and decision components
The skill identifies Profile 5: Sentinel for edge case detection
The skill identifies that the human review escalation path must be architecturally guaranteed, not optional
The skill proposes guardrails as hard constraints, not soft guidelines
The skill routes to Squad Topologies Architect + SAFe layer
The skill produces a squad-registry.md with explicit guardrails noted per squad
The skill notes the audit trail requirement in the design decisions log

evals.prompt: I want to summarize my weekly Notion notes every Friday at 5pm and send myself a digest email.
evals.expected_output: Correctly classified as Tier 0, Profile 0 (Assistant, scheduled variant). Agent Brief with scheduled trigger, Notion read access, email send, no approval gate needed (sending to self). Simple, fast, no over-engineering.
expectations: The skill classifies this as Tier 0 immediately — very simple case
The skill does NOT ask many clarifying questions — this is self-evident
The skill identifies Event-Driven (scheduled) execution strategy
The skill identifies RAG or direct API access for Notion
The skill produces an Agent Brief, not a squad topology
The Agent Brief has a scheduled trigger (Friday 5pm)
The Agent Brief notes Notion read access and email send as the only tools needed
The Agent Brief is concise — this is a simple agent, the brief should reflect that
The skill does not propose an approval gate since the agent is emailing the owner themselves

evals.prompt: We need to scrape product data from 100,000 e-commerce pages, extract structured attributes (price, SKU, description, availability), normalize it, deduplicate it, and load it into our data warehouse. It needs to run daily.
evals.expected_output: Correctly classified as Tier 1, Profile 6 (Swarm Unit) + unFIX augmentation for dynamic crew scaling. Squad Topologies provides the structure (ingestion, extraction, normalization, dedup, load squads or a simpler pipeline design). unFIX handles dynamic crew scaling for the crawl volume.
expectations: The skill classifies this as Tier 1 — this is not a single agent problem at 100k pages
The skill identifies Profile 6: Swarm Unit as the primary profile
The skill identifies unFIX as the relevant augmentation for dynamic crew scaling
The skill asks the LeSS question and correctly concludes one agent cannot handle 100k pages reliably
The skill identifies a pipeline structure: crawl → extract → normalize → dedup → load
The skill notes that the platform squad needs to handle shared state (dedup requires a seen-set)
The skill produces a squad-topology.diag
The skill notes daily scheduling as a trigger in the design
The skill identifies a Sentinel need for monitoring crawl success rates and pipeline health
